entries.name: Apify MCP Server
entries.use_for: Give agents access to thousands of ready-made scrapers and crawlers for social media, maps, e-commerce and websites.
entries.why: Official Apify server with hosted OAuth access; the broadest catalogue of web-data tools available over MCP.
entries.summary: Official Apify MCP server (mcp.apify.com) giving AI agents access to thousands of Apify Store scrapers and crawlers, with OAuth for clients like Claude.ai.
entries.best_for: Agents needing web data from social media, maps, search and e-commerce.
entries.not_for: Depends on the Apify platform and its pricing; third-party actors vary in quality.

entries.name: AWS MCP Servers
entries.use_for: Official MCP servers for AWS services, docs, CDK, cost and more
entries.why: AWS's own suite of MCP servers with broad service coverage
entries.summary: Suite of official MCP servers for AWS services, documentation, CDK and cost analysis. Notes that the Agent Toolkit for AWS is the successor.
entries.best_for: Agents working with AWS services and docs.
entries.not_for: README points to a successor toolkit, so check which suite is current; needs AWS credentials.

entries.name: Blender MCP
entries.use_for: Drive Blender from Claude and other agents for 3D modeling
entries.why: The most popular creative-tool MCP server
entries.summary: Third-party MCP integration that connects Blender to LLMs for prompt-assisted 3D modeling and scene manipulation. Formerly blender-mcp; PyPI package is mcp-for-blender.
entries.best_for: Letting Claude or other agents drive Blender scenes.
entries.not_for: Not made by Blender; needs a running Blender with the addon.

entries.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
entries.use_for: Let coding agents inspect and debug a live Chrome: DOM, console, network, performance traces.
entries.why: Official Chrome DevTools team server; best for debugging and performance work in agents.
entries.summary: MCP server letting coding agents control and inspect a live Chrome with DevTools capabilities such as DOM, console, network and performance traces.
entries.best_for: Browser debugging, performance analysis and automation by agents.
entries.not_for: Chrome only and needs a running browser; exposes live browser data.

entries.name: Claude Context
entries.use_for: Semantic code search over a whole codebase for coding agents
entries.why: Zilliz's MCP server that indexes code into a vector DB (Milvus/Zilliz) for hybrid search, cutting tokens for agents.
entries.summary: MCP server that indexes a codebase into a vector database (Milvus/Zilliz) for hybrid semantic code search, reducing tokens agents spend reading files.
entries.best_for: Agents searching large codebases semantically.
entries.not_for: Requires a vector DB and embeddings provider (Zilliz Cloud or Milvus), adding setup and cost.

entries.name: Cloudflare MCP Servers
entries.use_for: MCP servers for Cloudflare: Workers, observability, DNS, docs, browser rendering
entries.why: Official remote MCP servers from Cloudflare
entries.summary: Official remote MCP servers from Cloudflare covering Workers, observability, DNS, docs and browser rendering through natural language.
entries.best_for: Managing Cloudflare accounts from MCP clients.
entries.not_for: Cloudflare only; needs account authorization.

entries.name: code-review-graph
entries.use_for: Give AI coding tools a local code graph so they read only the files a change touches.
entries.why: Builds a Tree-sitter graph of calls and imports and serves compact context over MCP.
entries.summary: code-review-graph parses your repo with Tree-sitter into a graph of functions, classes, imports, calls and test coverage, updated incrementally. An MCP server then returns the smallest set of files needed for a review. One install command configures many AI coding tools.
entries.best_for: Large repos where assistants waste tokens re-reading code during reviews.
entries.not_for: The README admits limits: tiny single-file edits can cost more than a plain read, search ranking needs work, and impact recall is circular.

entries.name: codebase-memory-mcp
entries.use_for: Give coding agents a persistent code knowledge graph via MCP
entries.why: High-performance MCP server indexing repos into a queryable graph (162 languages) so agents navigate code without re-reading files.
entries.summary: Local MCP server that indexes repositories into a queryable code knowledge graph across many languages, lowering token use and offering visualization.
entries.best_for: Giving agents persistent structural code context.
entries.not_for: Newer project; index must stay current and is language-parser dependent.

entries.name: Context7
entries.use_for: Feed agents up-to-date, version-specific library documentation via MCP.
entries.why: Widely used fix for outdated API knowledge in coding agents; official Upstash server.
entries.summary: MCP server that fetches current, version-specific library documentation and code examples and injects them into the coding agent's prompt (triggered by adding 'use context7'). Aims to avoid outdated or hallucinated APIs.
entries.best_for: Coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) working with fast-moving frameworks and SDKs where training data is stale.
entries.not_for: Not a general web search or private-docs indexer; relies on the Context7 hosted index and its coverage of public libraries.

entries.name: Desktop Commander MCP
entries.use_for: Give Claude terminal control, file search and diff-based editing
entries.why: Popular MCP server for local shell commands, long-running processes, file search and surgical edits.
entries.summary: MCP server giving AI clients terminal control with interactive process management, file reading/search, diff-based editing, in-memory code execution (Python, Node, R), and Excel/PDF handling. Also offers a remote MCP option.
entries.best_for: Letting Claude Desktop or other MCP clients run shell commands, edit files surgically and analyze local CSV/JSON/Excel data.
entries.not_for: Grants broad local shell and filesystem access, so a security risk on shared or sensitive machines; not a sandboxed execution environment.

entries.name: DevSpace
entries.use_for: Let ChatGPT or Claude read, edit and run code in your local projects through a self-hosted MCP server.
entries.why: Turns ChatGPT into a coding agent on your own machine without uploading files.
entries.summary: A self-hosted MCP server exposing tools to read, write and edit files, search code, run shell commands and use Git worktrees inside approved folders. It follows AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md and finds local skills. You expose it through your own tunnel.
entries.best_for: Using ChatGPT or another MCP-capable chat host as a coding agent on a local repo.
entries.not_for: Offline use: a public HTTPS tunnel is needed for hosted chat apps. It runs real commands on your machine, so approve folders carefully.

entries.name: Draw.io MCP Server
entries.use_for: Let LLMs create and open diagrams in draw.io from Claude, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients.
entries.why: Official draw.io server with a hosted endpoint, inline diagram viewer and a no-install option.
entries.summary: The official draw.io MCP server. It offers an MCP App server that shows diagrams inline in chat, a tool server (`npx @drawio/mcp`) that opens diagrams in the editor from XML, CSV or Mermaid, assistant plugins and Claude Project instructions.
entries.best_for: Anyone who wants an AI assistant to produce editable draw.io diagrams.
entries.not_for: Diagram creation only. Inline rendering needs a host that supports MCP Apps.

entries.name: Engram
entries.use_for: Give any MCP-compatible coding agent persistent memory across sessions.
entries.why: A single Go binary with SQLite and FTS5 and no other dependencies.
entries.summary: Engram is a single Go binary that stores what an agent learns in SQLite with full-text search. It offers an MCP server, HTTP API, CLI and a terminal UI to browse memories. It has setup targets for 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
entries.best_for: Stopping coding agents from forgetting your project between sessions, with local storage.
entries.not_for: Stores notes and recalls by text search, not a vector database. The Engram name and logo are trademarks of the author.

entries.name: Exa MCP Server
entries.use_for: Give agents web search and crawling via the Exa search API.
entries.why: Official Exa server, also offered as a hosted remote endpoint.
entries.summary: MCP server connecting agents to Exa's search API for web search, content fetching and multi-step research. Distributed as an agent plugin and a hosted MCP endpoint, installable in Claude, Codex and other clients.
entries.best_for: Agents needing neural web search and page content retrieval through MCP.
entries.not_for: Requires an Exa API key and is tied to the paid Exa service; not a self-hosted search engine.

entries.name: Executor
entries.use_for: Set up tools, auth and per-tool policies once and share them with every MCP-compatible agent.
entries.why: One catalog of MCP, OpenAPI and GraphQL integrations with allow, approval or block policies per tool.
entries.summary: Executor is an integration layer for AI agents. You add MCP servers, OpenAPI specs or GraphQL APIs, set credentials and policies once, and any MCP-compatible agent uses the same catalog. Runs as a local CLI, desktop app, hosted cloud, or self-hosted on Docker or Cloudflare.
entries.best_for: You use several agents (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT) and want one place for API keys, tool catalog and approval rules.
entries.not_for: Not an agent framework. Agents must speak MCP to use it. Hosted cloud is a separate product from the self-hosted option.

entries.name: FastMCP
entries.use_for: Pythonic framework for building MCP servers and clients quickly.
entries.why: Most popular high-level Python MCP framework; adds auth, composition, proxying and testing.
entries.summary: Python framework for building MCP servers, clients and interactive apps. Tools are declared as ordinary decorated Python functions, with schemas, validation and transport handled by the framework.
entries.best_for: Python developers who want to expose functions or APIs to LLMs as MCP tools quickly, with less boilerplate than the raw SDK.
entries.not_for: Python only; if your stack is TypeScript use an MCP TypeScript framework instead.

entries.name: Firecrawl MCP Server
entries.use_for: Add web scraping, crawling and search to agents through Firecrawl.
entries.why: Official Firecrawl server; returns clean markdown from pages for LLM use.
entries.summary: MCP server exposing Firecrawl's web search, scraping, crawling, page interaction and deep-research features to agents, returning clean structured content. Includes search over an index of GitHub issues, PRs and docs.
entries.best_for: Agents that need to read arbitrary live web pages or crawl sites into LLM-ready markdown/JSON.
entries.not_for: Depends on the Firecrawl API (key and usage-based pricing); not a standalone local scraper.

entries.name: Framelink Figma MCP
entries.use_for: Feed Figma layout data to coding agents for design-to-code
entries.why: Widely used Figma MCP for one-shot UI implementation
entries.summary: MCP server that fetches Figma file, frame or group data via the Figma API and passes simplified layout and style info to coding agents like Cursor. Gives better design-to-code results than pasted screenshots.
entries.best_for: Implementing Figma designs in any framework using an AI coding agent from a shared Figma link.
entries.not_for: Read-only access to Figma data; needs a Figma API token and does not edit designs or generate Figma files.

entries.name: Gemini Notebook MCP & CLI
entries.use_for: Drive Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) from the command line or from AI assistants over MCP.
entries.why: One package gives both an nlm CLI and an MCP server, with encrypted login storage in the OS keychain.
entries.summary: A Python CLI and MCP server for Gemini Notebook. It lists and creates notebooks, adds sources from URLs, text, Drive and files, and queries notebooks. nlm setup connects the tools to your AI assistants.
entries.best_for: Scripting NotebookLM-style research or letting an agent manage notebooks and sources.
entries.not_for: Official API stability. It signs in with a Google account, and Enterprise support is experimental.

entries.name: GhidraMCP
entries.use_for: Let LLMs drive Ghidra to decompile and analyze binaries
entries.why: Ghidra plugin plus MCP bridge exposing decompilation, renaming and xrefs to agents for autonomous reverse engineering.
entries.summary: Ghidra plugin plus MCP server that lets LLMs decompile and analyze binaries, list methods, classes, imports and exports, and automatically rename functions and data.
entries.best_for: AI-assisted reverse engineering of native binaries inside Ghidra.
entries.not_for: Requires a running Ghidra install with the plugin; limited to what Ghidra exposes and not for dynamic or runtime analysis.

entries.name: GitHub MCP Server
entries.use_for: Give agents access to GitHub repos, issues, PRs and Actions through MCP.
entries.why: GitHub's official server, available locally or as a hosted remote server.
entries.summary: GitHub's official MCP server that lets agents read repos and code, manage issues and pull requests, analyze code and automate workflows through natural language. Available as a hosted endpoint or local server.
entries.best_for: Giving AI assistants authenticated access to GitHub repos, issues, PRs and Actions.
entries.not_for: GitHub only; needs a token with appropriate scopes, and write tools carry risk if broad permissions are granted.

entries.name: Godot AI
entries.use_for: Letting an MCP client like Claude Code build scenes, edit nodes and scripts, and wire signals in a live Godot editor.
entries.why: Exposes 46 tools and 120+ operations covering UI, materials, animation, particles and environments.
entries.summary: Godot AI is an MCP server that bridges MCP clients to a running Godot editor through a local Python server and an editor plugin, both authenticated. It fully supports GDScript (parse-validated, hot-reloaded) and offers text-only support for C# scripts.
entries.best_for: Godot 4.7+ developers who want an AI assistant to build and edit scenes directly in the live editor.
entries.not_for: Does not build or report compiler errors for C# scripts; those still need the editor's Build panel or dotnet build.

entries.name: Google MCP
entries.use_for: Find Google's official MCP servers and examples for deploying MCP servers to Google Cloud.
entries.why: Official index of Google's remote and open-source MCP servers with deployment guidance and sample agents.
entries.summary: A repository listing Google's official Model Context Protocol servers: managed remote ones such as BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Firestore and Maps, and open-source ones such as Workspace, Firebase, GKE and MCP Toolbox for Databases. It also links deployment guides for Cloud Run and has two example apps.
entries.best_for: Connecting agents to Google Cloud and Google products through supported MCP servers.
entries.not_for: Mostly an index and guidance. The servers themselves live elsewhere, and examples are small.

entries.name: ha-mcp
entries.use_for: Let an AI assistant control Home Assistant and manage its automations, scripts and dashboards.
entries.why: Wide tool coverage plus safety controls such as read-only mode and automatic edit backups.
entries.summary: An unofficial MCP server for Home Assistant. AI assistants can search entities, control devices, and create or edit automations, scripts, helpers and dashboards. It also reads history and traces, handles backups, and includes a read-only mode, per-tool enable switches and approval policies.
entries.best_for: Home Assistant users who want to manage their setup by chatting with Claude or another MCP client.
entries.not_for: Unofficial. Home Assistant also ships its own built-in MCP server, built on Assist, which is a narrower option.

entries.name: iPhone Use
entries.use_for: Let Codex or another agent drive a real iPhone over USB: open apps, read screens, tap and type.
entries.why: Local MCP server on WebDriverAgent with a live screen view and screenshot fallback when controls fail.
entries.summary: iPhone Use gives agents hands on a real iPhone. It uses WebDriverAgent on the phone, a local MCP service, setup and usage skills, and a live screen widget. It supports Codex, and adapted installs for WorkBuddy and Doubao. The README is mainly in Chinese.
entries.best_for: You want an agent to automate apps on your own iPhone and can use a Mac with Xcode.
entries.not_for: Needs macOS, full Xcode, a USB iPhone, and your own signed WDA runner. The README says the repo is private and needs access. Sends anonymous usage stats by default in Codex.

entries.name: Jarvis Registry
entries.use_for: Put one secure gateway in front of your MCP servers and agents with identity and per-tool access control.
entries.why: Combines an MCP gateway, A2A agent registry, OAuth/OIDC login and tool-level ACLs.
entries.summary: An enterprise MCP and A2A gateway and registry. It proxies MCP over SSE or Streamable HTTP, signs users in via Keycloak, Cognito or Entra ID, enforces scope and role rules down to single tools, and offers discovery and observability.
entries.best_for: Companies that need governed access for copilots and agents to internal tools.
entries.not_for: Heavy for a single-user or hobby setup. It manages access to MCP servers rather than being a tool server itself.

entries.name: MCP Inspector
entries.use_for: Visually test and debug MCP servers
entries.why: Official dev tool for building and debugging MCP servers

license_verified.note: Apache-2.0; some older contributions remain MIT during MCP relicensing

entries.summary: Developer tool for testing and debugging MCP servers, offering a web UI, a scriptable CLI, a terminal UI and an experimental connection CLI.
entries.best_for: Interactively exploring and testing an MCP server's tools, resources and prompts during development or in CI.
entries.not_for: A debugging tool, not a runtime client or framework for production agents.

entries.name: MCP Python SDK
entries.use_for: Official Python SDK for building MCP servers and clients.
entries.why: The reference Python SDK, including the FastMCP-style decorator API.
entries.summary: Official Python SDK for the Model Context Protocol, for building MCP servers and clients that expose tools, resources and prompts to LLM applications.
entries.best_for: Python projects implementing MCP servers or clients on the official SDK.
entries.not_for: Lower-level than FastMCP-style frameworks; Python only.

entries.name: MCP reference servers
entries.use_for: Reference MCP servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory and more) maintained by the MCP project.
entries.why: Official reference implementations; the canonical examples for building and testing servers.
entries.summary: Collection of reference MCP server implementations (filesystem, git, fetch, memory and others) maintained by the MCP steering group, plus links to community servers.
entries.best_for: Learning MCP by example or using basic filesystem, git or fetch servers as starting points.
entries.not_for: The README says these are reference implementations, not production-ready solutions; the registry is the place to find published servers.

entries.name: MCP Toolbox for Databases
entries.use_for: MCP server exposing Postgres, MySQL, BigQuery, AlloyDB and more as safe tools
entries.why: Google's open-source database MCP server with many backends
entries.summary: Open-source MCP server for databases such as Postgres, MySQL, BigQuery and AlloyDB. Offers prebuilt generic tools for schema exploration and queries, and a framework for defining custom tools with pooling and auth.
entries.best_for: Connecting AI agents or IDEs to enterprise databases safely, or building custom database tools for agents.
entries.not_for: Heavier than a simple DB driver wrapper; best suited to the supported database list, with Google-oriented ecosystem ties.

entries.name: MCP TypeScript SDK
entries.use_for: Official TypeScript SDK for building MCP servers and clients.
entries.why: The reference SDK most JS/TS MCP servers are built on.
entries.summary: Official TypeScript SDK (v2 on main) for building MCP servers and clients, implementing the current MCP spec. v1.x remains on a separate branch with security fixes.
entries.best_for: TypeScript/Node projects building MCP servers or clients with the official SDK.
entries.not_for: v2 has a migration path from v1 and different package names; lower-level than full-stack MCP frameworks.

entries.name: mcp-use
entries.use_for: Full-stack framework for building MCP servers, MCP Apps and connecting agents to any MCP server.
entries.why: Covers both client and server side with SDKs for TS and Python; handy for MCP Apps in ChatGPT/Claude.
entries.summary: TypeScript full-stack framework for building MCP servers, MCP Apps and ChatGPT/Claude connectors, with typed APIs, built-in Inspector, and tooling to connect agents to MCP servers.
entries.best_for: TypeScript teams wanting a batteries-included framework with views, inspector and deployment for MCP servers.
entries.not_for: TypeScript-centric and a framework layer on top of MCP; v2 requires migration from v1.

entries.name: MCPorter
entries.use_for: Call any MCP server's tools from a terminal, a TypeScript script, or a generated standalone CLI.
entries.why: Lets scripts and agents use MCP tools directly, with typed clients and one-off URL or stdio connections.
entries.summary: A TypeScript runtime and CLI for discovering and calling Model Context Protocol servers. You can list a server's tools, call them from the command line, connect to ad-hoc URLs or stdio commands, and generate typed clients or standalone CLIs.
entries.best_for: Developers and agents that need MCP tools outside an MCP-enabled chat client.
entries.not_for: It is a client, not an MCP server. Needs Node 24 or newer for npm installs.

entries.name: n8n-mcp
entries.use_for: Let Claude, Cursor etc. design and build n8n workflows
entries.why: MCP server exposing n8n node docs, properties and validation so agents can generate working n8n workflows.
entries.summary: MCP server giving AI assistants structured knowledge of n8n's workflow nodes (3,000+ core and community), their properties and operations, so they can design and build n8n workflows.
entries.best_for: Letting Claude or Cursor design, validate and build n8n automations accurately.
entries.not_for: Specific to n8n; it supplies node knowledge, not a workflow runtime, and it is a third-party project.

entries.name: OpenConnector
entries.use_for: Give AI agents authenticated access to 1,000+ SaaS apps through SDK, CLI, MCP or HTTP.
entries.why: A self-hostable alternative to Pipedream and Composio with a shared catalog of prebuilt actions.
entries.summary: OpenConnector is an open-source connector gateway for AI agents. It handles OAuth and API-key credentials, exposes provider actions with schemas, and enforces scopes and allow/block policies with run logs. Run it with Docker or Node.js, or use the hosted runtime.
entries.best_for: Agent builders who want one integration layer across many SaaS tools without writing OAuth code.
entries.not_for: You manage storage and your own OAuth apps if you self-host. Hosted use depends on OOMOL's service.

entries.name: Playwright MCP
entries.use_for: Let agents drive a real browser via Playwright using accessibility snapshots.
entries.why: Official Microsoft server; structured page snapshots instead of screenshots make it reliable and cheap.
entries.summary: MCP server for browser automation using Playwright, where agents interact with pages through structured accessibility snapshots rather than screenshots.
entries.best_for: Agents that need to navigate and interact with real web pages through an MCP client.
entries.not_for: README notes coding agents may prefer the Playwright CLI plus skills for token efficiency; not a test-runner replacement.

entries.name: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)
entries.use_for: MCP server that lets agents reverse engineer apps and native binaries, from runtime behaviour down to disassembly.
entries.why: One of the most popular MCP projects; unique coverage of binaries, Electron apps and runtime tracing.
entries.summary: MCP server that lets agents reverse engineer apps and native binaries, from runtime behaviour down to disassembly, driving tools such as Ghidra, JADX and firmware and Electron analysis.
entries.best_for: Agent-driven reverse engineering of native, Android, Electron or firmware targets.
entries.not_for: Heavy toolchain prerequisites (Ghidra, JADX); not for ordinary source-code architecture analysis.

entries.name: Repowise
entries.use_for: Give coding agents and humans an index of a codebase: call graph, risk, dead code and past decisions.
entries.why: Risk, health and dead-code checks make no LLM calls, so the same diff gives the same answer.
entries.summary: Repowise indexes code, call graph, git history, tests and docs once on your machine. You and your agent then ask what calls what, what breaks on a change and what is dead, via CLI, REST or MCP. It can also gate changes in CI with SARIF.
entries.best_for: Agents or teams working in a large repo who want to stop paying tokens to rediscover the code every session.
entries.not_for: AGPL-3.0 licence, with a commercial option. Free use is described for one developer. Not a general search engine for non-code data.

entries.name: Semble
entries.use_for: Give coding agents fast natural-language code search over a repo, as an MCP server, CLI or sub-agent.
entries.why: Runs on CPU with no API keys and returns only relevant snippets instead of whole files.
entries.summary: Semble is a code search library for agents. It indexes a repo in about half a second and answers natural-language queries with just the relevant snippets. It installs as an MCP server, AGENTS.md instructions or a sub-agent.
entries.best_for: Cutting token use when a coding agent searches a codebase, without GPUs, API keys or external services.
entries.not_for: Not a general document search or a hosted service. It is built for code search by agents, and setup assumes uv and a supported coding agent.

entries.name: Serena
entries.use_for: Give coding agents semantic, LSP-backed code navigation and editing via MCP
entries.why: Highly adopted MCP toolkit that adds IDE-like symbol tools to any agent

license_verified.note: Serena app GPL-3.0-or-later; bundled SolidLSP MIT

entries.summary: Coding-agent toolkit exposing IDE-like semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring and debugging at the symbol level via language servers (LSP), usable through MCP in any client.
entries.best_for: Giving coding agents precise symbol-level navigation and edits in medium to large codebases.
entries.not_for: Needs language servers set up per language; extra overhead for tiny projects or one-off scripts.

entries.name: SocratiCode
entries.use_for: Give an AI coding assistant semantic search, dependency graphs and impact analysis over a large local codebase.
entries.why: Runs locally with zero setup, and covers hybrid search, polyglot dependency graphs and symbol-level impact analysis.
entries.summary: A codebase context engine used as an MCP server or plugin. It indexes your code with hybrid semantic search, builds dependency graphs and call flows, and adds searchable context such as database schemas and API specs.
entries.best_for: Letting Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code understand a big or multi-project codebase without sending code to the cloud.
entries.not_for: Needs Node.js 18.17+ and Docker for the default local Qdrant and Ollama stack. AGPL-3.0 licensed, which limits closed-source reuse.

entries.name: Supabase MCP
entries.use_for: Let agents manage Supabase projects: SQL, migrations, logs, edge functions
entries.why: Supabase's maintained MCP server
entries.summary: Official Supabase MCP server letting AI assistants manage projects: run SQL, apply migrations, view logs and advisors, manage edge functions and fetch config.
entries.best_for: Developers using Cursor or Claude to build against Supabase projects.
entries.not_for: Supabase only; gives agents powerful database access, so use dev projects or read-only mode and not production data.

entries.name: TradingView MCP Bridge
entries.use_for: Let Claude Code control a local TradingView Desktop app for chart analysis and Pine Script work.
entries.why: Drives your own TradingView Desktop over Chrome DevTools Protocol; it does not touch TradingView's servers.
entries.summary: An MCP bridge to your locally running TradingView Desktop. It can change symbols and timeframes, read indicator values, draw on charts, and write, compile and debug Pine Script.
entries.best_for: Pine Script development and chart workflow automation by someone with a TradingView subscription.
entries.not_for: Executing trades, or use without a TradingView subscription and Desktop app. It relies on undocumented internals that can break on updates.

entries.name: Unity MCP
entries.use_for: Let AI assistants control the Unity Editor: assets, scenes, scripts.
entries.why: The most used Unity bridge for agents, actively maintained with many contributors.
entries.summary: Unity package plus Python MCP bridge that lets AI assistants control the Unity Editor: create scenes and GameObjects, edit C# scripts, manage assets, run tests, profile and build.
entries.best_for: Unity developers who want an AI client to drive the editor in natural language.
entries.not_for: Unity Editor only (2021.3 to 6.x) and requires Python 3.10+; not for runtime or in-game AI.

entries.name: wigolo
entries.use_for: Give coding agents local web search, fetch, crawl and research over MCP with no API keys.
entries.why: Runs fully on your machine with no keys or per-query cost, and wires into many agents with one command.
entries.summary: wigolo gives an agent search, fetch, crawl, extract, cache, find-similar and research tools. It runs as an MCP server, a REST endpoint, or an SDK, and downloads a browser engine and local models on setup.
entries.best_for: Agents that need web access without paying for search APIs or sending queries to a cloud.
entries.not_for: Small installs: it needs Node 20+ and about 1.5 GB disk. It is a public beta under AGPL-3.0.

entries.name: xiaohongshu-mcp
entries.use_for: Search, read and publish Xiaohongshu (RED) posts from agents
entries.why: Widely used MCP server for Xiaohongshu: login, feed/search, post details and publishing image/video notes.
entries.summary: MCP server that lets AI assistants access Xiaohongshu (RedNote) data. It handles login and login-status checks and can publish image-and-text posts with titles, descriptions and images from URLs or local paths. Prebuilt binaries cover macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64 and Linux x64, and a Docker image is available.
entries.best_for: Letting an AI agent publish to or read from a Xiaohongshu account through MCP, for content automation on that platform.
entries.not_for: Other social platforms. macOS Intel and Linux ARM64 are unsupported, it needs a logged-in account, and the README is mostly Chinese; deployment can be finicky (the author points to a browser-plugin alternative).
